# Texas, Texas A&M rivalry takes center stage with SEC title hopes at stake
...
AUSTIN (KXAN) — What goes around comes around, especially during rivalry week in college football.

A year ago, Texas played spoiler, handing Texas A&M its first loss of the season with a 27-17 victory at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium. The Aggies entered undefeated, but left with an 11-1 record and a bitter ending to their regular season.

Now, the roles have reversed.

Texas enters this year’s showdown fighting to keep its SEC championship hopes alive, while the Aggies, already eliminated from bowl contention, have one final opportunity to ruin their rival’s plans.

For Steve Sarkisian, the stakes go well beyond the standings.

“This game divides households,” Sarkisian said. “These are the games that these guys talk about year-round.”

The rivalry, dating to 1894, returned in 2024 after a 13-year hiatus. For defensive back Justin Cryer, Saturday’s matchup is about representing generations of Longhorns.

“You’re playing for every single alumni and every single person who’s been involved,” Cryer said. “This means so much to so many people.”

Defensive lineman Lance Jackson knows Texas A&M has little left to play for beyond bragging rights, making the Aggies potentially even more dangerous.

“This basically is their bowl game,” Jackson said. “They’re going to put it all on the line.”

With rivalry games unfolding nationwide, Texas has one final regular-season challenge. The Longhorns spoiled the Aggies’ perfect season last year. Now, they’ll have to make sure history doesn’t repeat itself with the roles reversed.

That is virtually all the Aggies have left to play for as they wrap up a miserable season a year after reaching the CFP for the first time. Texas A&M enters the game having lost four in a row and with only four wins, Friday will be the team’s final game regardless of the outcome.
“Nothing’s going to erase what has happened,” Texas A&M coach Mike Elko said. “Nothing is going to change the results and the need to show massive improvement and fix where we’re at right now.
